title: Lights — Cabin Floor Marking — Installation of the Light-Emitting Diode Escape Path Strip
abstract: Installation of the low-current light-emitting diode floor proximity marking on aircraft carrying the photoluminescent standard, removing the charge time restriction that operators found unworkable.

sections.planning_reason: The photoluminescent standard removed the electrical load but introduced a charge time restriction that operators could not live with on dark overnight turnarounds, and two operators reverted at their own cost. A low-current light-emitting diode strip with a certified twelve-minute autonomy from distributed batteries gives the same weight and load benefit without the restriction. This Service Bulletin is written specifically for aircraft already at the photoluminescent standard, because the lining channel and the panel standoff introduced by that standard are reused.
sections.description: A continuous light-emitting diode strip is installed along the seat track cover line on both aisles and around each exit, powered from distributed battery units at four cabin stations. The exit marker assembly carries the local battery and the driver. The tubular spacers from the photoluminescent standard are retained to set the panel standoff. The bonded photoluminescent strip is removed and the channel is cleaned before the new strip is laid in.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Remove the cabin seats along both aisles and lift the aisle carpet in zones 291 and 951. De-energise the emergency lighting system. Remove the bonded photoluminescent strip and clean the lining channel to the surface standard given in the accomplishment instructions. Install the distributed battery units at the four cabin stations and route the low-current harness in the existing lining channel. Install the light-emitting diode strip and connect it at each station. Install the exit marker assemblies D3320137300785 and refit the tubular spacers AES27771-7A. Fit the new lenses at the exit panel 841LP7 and at the inboard stowage marker 850LP6. Do the emergency lighting functional test and the twelve-minute autonomy check. Remove the charge time placards. Refit the carpet and the seats and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00407 that are post MOD-163890 and still pre MOD-164122. Aircraft that never took the photoluminescent standard need a different work scope, because the lining channel does not exist and the powered floor marking wiring is still installed; those aircraft are covered by an individual quotation.
sections.material_note: Kit K3320-1064-01 contains the strip, the four battery units, the exit marker assemblies, the lenses and the harness. Lead time is twenty weeks and the battery units are the long-lead item. The removed photoluminescent strip is not returnable and is disposed of locally.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled cabin visit, or within 60 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
